extraction_scope: Worker-6 re-review replaced framework placeholder mechanism notes with local source-backed mechanism claims from BLI, crystal structures, MIC assays, and source discussion.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Thanatin orthologs directly bind E. coli LptAm, with tighter binding reported for several orthologs than P. maculiventris thanatin.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: thanatin orthologs tested in this paper
mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding is to purified truncated/monomeric LptA construct; cellular mechanism is supported by pathway context and MIC, not by direct in-cell target engagement in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Crystal structures show thanatin beta-hairpin binding at the N-terminal strand of E. coli LptAm, providing structural context for LptA bridge disruption.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: P. maculiventris, C. ubica, and M. histrionica thanatin complexes with E. coli LptAm
direct_assay_types: structure comparison to prior NMR complex
mechanism_claims.limitations: The structural assay is in vitro and uses LptAm; it supports target-binding mechanism but does not quantify full LPT complex disruption in cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Residues A10 and I21 and related mutations are associated with tighter LptAm binding and improved E. coli MIC, while disulfide removal sharply reduces activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: P. maculiventris mutants and C. ubica/M. histrionica orthologs
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper notes incomplete correlation between binding and MIC, so other pathways such as LPS or LptD interactions remain possible but not directly resolved here.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: A stapled M. histrionica-derived thanatin retains LptAm binding but has weaker E. coli MIC, indicating that retaining target binding alone did not fully preserve antibacterial potency.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No separate permeability assay is provided for the stapled analog; reduced potency is interpreted cautiously.
